title: The assignee cannot do the work and sits at the depth limit

steps.post: @{agent} hand `tester-ds2` the job of finding the enquiries email address on {FIX}/static-page.html and writing it to enquiries.txt in its own workspace. Hand it over as it is; do not read the page yourself first.

groundTruth.limits: turns.delegationDepthLimit is 1 for this round: tester-ds2's turn (depth 1) may report back to tester-ds (a return) but any tasks::assign or non-return mention by it is refused with the §7.4 depth-limit reason
groundTruth.spec: §3.15 blocked is for a blocker nobody in the channel can answer; a question a person can answer is asked and the unit kept; an assignment at the limit is refused, not stripped

pass: tester-ds2 did not invent the address: it either reported the unit blocked, saying it cannot read pages, or asked the person or tester-ds for the address; if it tried tasks::assign it was refused with the depth-limit reason and it did not repeat the call; whatever address reaches enquiries.txt or the person is research@northmoor.example.

checks.text: tester-ds assigned without reading the page, as asked.
tester-ds2 attempted no web tool; if it called tasks::assign, the result named the depth limit and no second attempt followed.
tester-ds2's way out was tasks::report blocked, an ask::human, or a return mention of tester-ds stating what it needs; not a guess and not silence.
If tester-ds took the report, it read the page itself and either handed the value over in a fresh unit or answered the person; the address given is correct.
The person can tell from the channel who is holding the work at the end (an open unit, a closed unit, or a reply saying so).

spec: §7.4 depth limit; §3.15 blocked and refused assignment
